newsitem.title: USA: Pratt wins Asiana engine contract.
newsitem.headline: Pratt wins Asiana engine contract.

text.p: Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp., said Monday it won an engine contract from Asiana Airlines to equip 48 new twin-engine Airbus Industrie A330 and Boeing 777 aircraft.
Pratt & Whitney gave no figure for the value of the contract, but industry analysts said the average cost per engine was about $10 million.
Pratt's PW4000 engine family will power all of the aircraft.
Pratt said the engines will be delivered between 1998 and 2006.
A Pratt spokesman told Reuters the total number of engines was more than 100, including spares.
Pratt said that before 1996, Asiana relied exclusively on General Electric Co.'s CF6-80C2 to power its widebody aircraft and on the CFM56 engine to power its narrowbody aircraft.
The new contract boosts Pratt's 1996 market share to 70 percent on the A330 and 43 percent on the 777, with an overall market share on the 777 of 42 percent and 53 percent on the A330, Pratt said.
